questions.q: What exactly triggers a position becoming eligible for liquidation?
options: The borrower requesting it voluntarily
The protocol team manually flagging the position
The loan reaching a fixed maturity date
Its health factor crossing below 1.0
questions.explain: Liquidation eligibility is purely a function of health factor crossing below 1.0 — no manual flagging or borrower action is involved.

questions.q: In the worked example, what happens to the health factor of a 1 ETH / 1,000 USDC-borrowed position (80% liquidation threshold) when ETH drops from 2,000 to 1,200 USDC?
options: It falls from 1.60 to 0.96, making the position eligible for liquidation
It rises from 1.60 to 1.96
It stays exactly at 1.60
It falls to exactly 0, wiping out the position entirely
questions.explain: Recomputing (1,200 * 0.80) / 1,000 = 0.96 — below 1.0, so the position becomes eligible for liquidation purely from the price move.

questions.q: Who actually carries out a liquidation on an eligible position?
options: Only the protocol's founding team
Any address — typically an automated bot — that calls the contract's public liquidate function
A government regulator overseeing the protocol
The original borrower, by choice
questions.explain: Liquidation is permissionless — any address can call the public liquidate function the moment a position is eligible, which in practice means competing bots.

options: A reward paid by the protocol team directly from its treasury
A penalty charged to the liquidator for participating
The extra collateral value (above the debt repaid) that a liquidator receives for performing the liquidation
An additional loan extended to the liquidator
questions.explain: Repaying 500 USDC of debt for 525 USDC of seized collateral at a 5% bonus gives the liquidator a 25 USDC profit — the economic incentive to act.

questions.q: Why is competition among liquidator bots actually good for a lending protocol's solvency?
options: It guarantees collateral prices never fall
It eliminates the need for any collateral at all
It slows down the liquidation process, giving borrowers more time
Fast, competitive liquidation prevents undercollateralized debt from piling up faster than it can be cleaned up, which would otherwise become bad debt the protocol absorbs
questions.explain: Because liquidation is permissionless and competitive, eligible positions tend to get cleaned up quickly — slow or discretionary liquidation would let bad debt accumulate instead.
